title: 복 타러 간 총각
titleT: The Boy Who Went to Seek His Fortune

pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 산 아래 작은 마을에 총각이 혼자 살았어요. 부지런하기로는 마을에서 으뜸이었지요. 해가 뜨기도 전에 괭이를 들고 밭을 갈고, 해가 져도 일손을 놓지 않았어요. 그런데 이상하게도 살림은 늘 그대로였답니다.
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a small village at the foot of a mountain, there lived a young man all by himself. Nobody in the village worked harder than he did. Before the sun was even up he took his hoe out to the field, and when the sun went down he still would not put his tools away. But strangely, no matter how hard he worked, he never had one bit more than before.

pages.ko: 어느 날 총각이 무릎을 탁 쳤어요. "그래! 서쪽 끝에 계신 신령님을 찾아가서, 내 복이 어디 있는지 여쭤보자!" 총각은 바짓가랑이에 대님을 단단히 매고, 새 미투리를 신고, 조롱박에 물을 가득 채웠어요. 괭이도 어깨에 척 걸쳐 메었지요. "복 타러 갑니다!"
pages.t: One day the young man slapped his knee. "That's it! I'll go to the Spirit who lives at the far western edge of the world, and ask him where my good fortune is!" He tied the cords tight around his trouser legs, put on a new pair of woven hemp shoes, and filled his little gourd bottle to the brim with water. He slung his hoe over his shoulder too. "I'm off to fetch my fortune!"

pages.ko: 한나절을 걸으니 길가에 커다란 감나무가 서 있었어요. "총각님, 어디 가시나요?" "신령님께 복을 타러 갑니다!" 그러자 나무가 가지를 축 늘어뜨렸어요. "저는 백 년이 되도록 꽃 한 송이 못 피웠어요. 제 것도 좀 여쭤봐 주세요!" "그럼요, 꼭 여쭤볼게요!"
pages.t: After walking half a day, he came to a great persimmon tree beside the road. "Where are you going, young man?" "I'm going to ask the Spirit where my fortune is!" At that, the tree let its branches droop. "I have stood here a hundred years and never grown a single blossom. Please ask about mine too!" "Of course! I'll be sure to ask!"

pages.ko: 이튿날, 물이 바싹 마른 우물가를 지나는데 커다란 물짐승이 고개를 쑤욱 내밀었어요. 몸집은 산더미만 한데 눈망울은 순하디순했지요. "저는 천 년을 기다렸는데도 하늘에 오르지 못해요. 제 것도 좀 여쭤봐 주세요!" "그럼요, 꼭 여쭤볼게요!"
pages.t: The next day, as he passed a well that had dried right up, a huge water creature poked its head out. Its body was as big as a mountain, but its eyes were as gentle as could be. "I have waited a thousand years, and still I cannot rise into the sky. Please ask about mine too!" "Of course! I'll be sure to ask!"

pages.ko: 산모퉁이 외딴집에서는 처녀가 마루에 앉아 자꾸만 눈물을 훔치고 있었어요. "저는 날마다 눈물이 나요. 어떻게 해야 웃을 수 있을까요? 제 것도 좀 여쭤봐 주세요!" "그럼요, 꼭 여쭤볼게요!" 총각은 손가락을 하나, 둘, 셋 꼽아 두었답니다.
pages.t: At a lonely house round the bend of the mountain, a young woman sat on the wooden porch, wiping her eyes again and again. "Tears come every single day. What must I do to smile? Please ask about mine too!" "Of course! I'll be sure to ask!" And the young man counted them off on his fingers — one, two, three.

pages.ko: 총각은 걷고 또 걸었어요. 미투리가 다 닳고, 조롱박의 물도 바닥이 났지요. 산을 몇 개나 넘었을까요. 걷다 보니 드디어 해가 지는 서쪽 끝, 구름이 걸린 봉우리에 닿았답니다.
pages.t: On and on he walked. His hemp shoes wore right through, and the water in his gourd bottle ran dry. How many mountains did he climb? At last he came to the far western edge where the sun goes down, and stood on a peak with clouds caught around it.

pages.ko: 구름 위 너럭바위에 하얀 수염 신령님이 앉아 계셨어요. "먼 길을 왔구나. 그런데 나는 한 사람에게 딱 세 가지만 답해 줄 수 있단다." 세 가지라니! 총각은 그만 말문이 막혔어요. 제 복을 여쭈면 약속 하나를 못 지키게 되니까요.
pages.t: High above the clouds, on a wide flat rock, sat the Spirit with his long white beard. "You have come a long way. But I may answer only three questions for any one person." Only three! The young man could not think what to say. If he asked about his own fortune, he would have to break one of his promises.

pages.ko: 총각은 잠깐 눈을 감았다가, 꼽아 두었던 손가락을 하나씩 폈어요. "감나무는 왜 꽃이 못 필까요? 물짐승은 왜 하늘에 못 오를까요? 처녀는 왜 눈물이 그치지 않을까요?" 세 가지를 다 쓰고 나니 제 복은 여쭐 수 없었지요. 그래도 총각은 고개를 끄덕였어요. "꼭 여쭤보겠다고 약속했거든요."
pages.t: The young man closed his eyes for a moment. Then he opened up his counted fingers, one by one. "Why can the persimmon tree grow no blossoms? Why can the water creature not rise into the sky? Why do the young woman's tears never stop?" With all three questions used up, there was none left for his own fortune. Still, the young man nodded. "I promised I would ask."

pages.ko: 신령님이 껄껄 웃으며 답해 주었어요. "감나무 뿌리 밑에 금덩이가 눌러 있단다. 파내 주면 꽃이 필 테고, 그 금은 파낸 사람이 갖거라. 물짐승은 여의주를 둘이나 물었으니 하나를 착한 이에게 주면 하늘에 오른단다. 처녀는 마음 나눌 짝을 만나면 눈물이 웃음으로 바뀌지." 그러곤 빙그레 덧붙였어요. "네 복도 벌써 다 일러 주었단다."
pages.t: The Spirit laughed a great, rumbling laugh and gave his answers. "Under the persimmon tree's roots, a lump of gold is pressing down. Dig it out and the tree will blossom — and whoever digs it up may keep the gold. The water creature holds two wish-granting pearls in its mouth; if it gives one to a kind person, it will rise into the sky. And the young woman's tears will turn to laughter when she meets someone to share her heart with." Then he added with a twinkle, "And I have already told you where your own fortune is."

pages.ko: 돌아오는 길, 총각은 외딴집부터 들렀어요. "마음 나눌 짝을 만나면 웃게 된대요!" 처녀가 고개를 들자 눈물이 뚝 그쳤어요. "그 착한 사람이… 총각님이면 좋겠어요." 두 사람은 볼이 발그레해져서, 나란히 길을 걷기 시작했답니다.
pages.t: On the way home, the young man stopped at the lonely house first. "They say you'll smile when you meet someone to share your heart with!" The young woman lifted her head, and her tears stopped at once. "I hope that kind person… is you." Both their cheeks turned pink, and the two of them set off down the road side by side.

pages.ko: 마른 우물가에 다다르자 총각이 두 손을 모아 외쳤어요. "여의주를 하나만 착한 이에게 주세요!" 물짐승이 빙그레 웃었어요. "그 착한 이가 바로 총각님이지요." 물짐승은 반짝이는 여의주 하나를 총각의 손바닥에 톡 놓아 주었어요. 그러자 몸이 스르르 떠올라 구름 사이로 훨훨— 마침내 하늘에 올랐답니다.
pages.t: When they reached the dried-up well, the young man cupped his hands and called out, "Please give one of your pearls to a kind person!" The water creature smiled. "That kind person is you, of course." And it set one shining wish-granting pearl gently in the palm of his hand. Then its great body floated slowly up, up between the clouds — and at last it rose into the sky!

pages.ko: 감나무 앞에 다다른 총각은 어깨의 괭이를 내렸어요. 쿵! 쿵! 쿵! 뿌리 밑을 파 내려가자 흙 속에서 누런 금덩이가 데굴 굴러 나왔지요. "아이고 시원해라, 이제야 숨이 트여요!" 감나무가 기지개를 켰답니다.
pages.t: When he came to the persimmon tree, the young man lifted the hoe down off his shoulder. Thump! Thump! Thump! He dug deep beneath the roots, and out of the earth rolled a lump of yellow gold. "Oh, what a relief — now I can breathe at last!" The persimmon tree gave a great big stretch.

pages.ko: 그 순간, 앙상하던 가지마다 하얀 감꽃이 팡! 팡! 팡! 눈처럼 피어났어요. 총각의 발치에는 금덩이가, 손에는 여의주가, 곁에는 처녀가 있었지요. 남의 복을 여쭈러 갔던 자리에, 제 복이 세 가지나 와 있었답니다.
pages.t: And that very moment, white persimmon blossoms burst open on every bare branch — pop! pop! pop! — like falling snow. At his feet lay the gold, in his hand shone the pearl, and beside him stood the young woman. He had gone to ask about other people's fortune, and three fortunes of his own were waiting for him there.

pages.ko: 마을로 돌아온 총각은 이웃들과 곡식을 나누고, 마른 우물도 새로 팠어요. 마을 사람들이 물었지요. "그래, 복은 대체 어디서 타 왔소?" 총각은 빙그레 웃었어요. "남의 것을 여쭈러 갔더니, 제 것이 따라왔지 뭐예요." 남을 돕는 마음이 곧 제 복이 된대요.
pages.t: Back in the village, the young man shared his grain with his neighbours and dug the dried-up well out fresh and new. The village people asked him, "So tell us — where in the world did you fetch your fortune from?" The young man only smiled. "I went to ask about other people's, and my own came following after." A heart that helps others, they say, becomes its own good fortune.
